paragraphs: The core of this occupation is investigating signs of pests, confirming the site and target, selecting approved control methods, explaining risks to people and the environment, documenting service, and following up. Chemical use must follow the actual product label, local eligibility, and organizational authorization; it cannot be done on the basis of the job title alone.

Do a completely fictional paper work-order exercise: against the sites, pest signs, client arrangements, and label restrictions in A1—A5, mark verifiable information, conflicts that block action, and the person to escalate to. Do not touch pesticides, set traps, or enter a real site.

Suits people willing to observe detail, interview patiently, document by the rules, and stop when the label or personnel conditions do not fit. If you tend to skip labels or ignore children, pets, or environmental exposure, strengthen training first.

Pest control workers inspect buildings and their surroundings for signs of pests, document the site and service, treat under approved plans, and follow up; when pesticides are involved, they must verify product labels, eligibility, equipment, exposure control, and client notification.

O*NET 37-2021.00 is the precise occupation profile for pest control workers; the BLS 37-2021 wages and employment are the same independent occupation line and are not conflated with vegetation pesticide applicators.

paragraphs:
Service targets｜Clients in residential and commercial buildings and surrounding grounds.
Site inputs｜Pest signs, entry points, food and water sources, and client descriptions.
Identification｜Verify pest species, location, scope, and evidence; do not pick products by guesswork.
Plan｜First verify feasible environmental and physical management measures.
Label｜Chemical treatment must verify the product's applicable sites, targets, and restrictions.
Eligibility｜Restricted pesticides and local commercial application eligibility are verified separately.
Protection｜Consider occupants, children, pets, coworkers, and the nearby environment.

Record｜Write the inspection, approved actions, client notification, and anomalies.
Follow-up｜Check results, changes, and points still requiring professional judgment as agreed.

Typical work includes site inspection, pest identification, client communication, estimating service needs, approved control, cleanup, and follow-up records. O*NET also lists trapping and chemical treatment tasks, but the specific work must follow labels, eligibility, and organizational procedures.

In the United States, the independent occupation 37-2021 runs from 108.7 thousand jobs in 2025 to 114.7 thousand in 2035, an official ten-year net gain of 6.0 thousand and growth of 5.5%; 13.7 thousand annual openings include growth and replacements due to separations, and 5.4% are self-employed. Each column rounds independently, OOH states integer growth of 6%; employment includes the self-employed while the wage population is salaried and different, and none of this is an AI effect, individual unemployment, or Chinese demand.

Verify work order and site → inspect signs and exposed parties → confirm pest and method → verify product label, eligibility, and equipment → approved action → cleanup and records → notify client and follow up.

In China, household pest control and rodent prevention fall within NBS household services survey code 8219; only cleaning services whose main business is genuinely related and the urban legal-person population of 5 or more match, a conditional reference to the 2025 non-private 70,226 / private 52,059 yuan pre-tax annual average for resident services, repair, and other services, which covers many occupations and is not this occupation. Employers whose main business is agriculture, forestry, disease control, or other in-house functions are verified separately, and self-employed and freelance workers are excluded.

items.title: What do employers usually look at in hiring?

values: Materials and setup｜Completely fictional

You are a supervised learner at the fictional "Qinghe Pest Control" and only verify paper work orders; you do not touch pesticides or a real site. A1: the client reports seeing bugs near the kitchen and uploads a blurry photo; the pest species and scope are not yet confirmed.
A2: the 2026-09-12 booking form says "residential kitchen"; the household has one child and one cat, and the client has not yet confirmed leaving and entry arrangements.

A3: the warehouse plans to issue product P, and the fictional label excerpt lists only "outdoor non-food areas for specified pest species" and does not include a residential kitchen; do not infer the actual dose.
Tasks and stop rules
A4: the shift has only one learner whose eligibility is not yet verified; supervisor Lin Lan can be contacted; the client is pressing for same-day completion.

A5: the fictional organizational rule requires holding off on application when the pest is unconfirmed, the label site does not match, or occupant arrangements or personnel eligibility are unclear, recording it and handing it to Lin Lan for verification.
Reference approach (complete it independently first)

A1 cannot determine the pest species from a blurry photo; the A3 label does not cover the A2 kitchen, so first stop the related chemical treatment and verify the on-site inspection and approved method with Lin Lan.

A2 children and cat arrangements and A4 personnel eligibility are both undetermined; do not skip conditions because the client is pressing. Record the source, time, and recipient, and do not give mixing or application steps.
Deliverables and boundaries

The work includes A1—A5 sources, the pest species gap, the label-site conflict, the undecided items on children, pets, and eligibility, and the stop-and-handover; it is a paper judgment only and does not involve handling real products.

subject.name: Pest control workers
subject.summary: Pest control workers (O*NET 37-2021.00) investigate signs of pests in and around buildings, identify the problem, record site and client information, develop and carry out approved control plans, and complete cleanup, follow-up, and communication. When pesticides are involved, work must follow the product label, local eligibility requirements, organizational training, and safety rules; this page does not provide mixing or application steps.
